fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Night-time driver confusion at a HAWK display is a recognized, site-specific safety issue with direct pedestrian-exposure consequences, making it substantive for a final-design-stage audit.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-US-001 provides a verbatim quote ('Drivers may be confused by competing background visual elements at night') that directly supports the pivotal claim, exceeding registry-id-only citation.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern with no normative/compliance claim conflated in, consistent with FHWA RSA semantics where conspicuity issues are safety observations.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Reflective border installation is specific, actionable, and a viable standard countermeasure for improving signal-head discrimination against night backgrounds; not a null recommendation.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians explicitly identified as the exposed vulnerable users if drivers misread or detect the display late, tying driver conspicuity to pedestrian protection.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance timing adequate for slower walkers at high-collision-frequency HAWK sites is a real, substantive final-design-stage safety issue affecting conflict exposure.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Verbatim quote in EV-US-016 ('The pedestrian clearance interval may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians') directly supports the pivotal claim and is tied to the recorded case-study issue for these exact sites.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety concern under FHWA RSA semantics with no compliance question conflated into it, and verification of assumed walking speeds is an appropriate final-design-stage audit query.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Reprogramming clearance intervals at all six named sites using a reduced assumed walking speed is specific, actionable, and viable before signal timing is finalized.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and elderly pedestrians are explicitly identified as affected road users and are the central focus of the finding, fully satisfying VRU consideration.
